Picks and Parlays NFL handicapper Steve Seagrave breaks down his top NFL player prop picks for Week 4 across several of the biggest games on the schedule. This week’s NFL prop bets feature quarterback, running back, wide receiver and anytime touchdown props , including passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and touchdown scorer markets. Whether you’re searching for NFL Week 4 player props, NFL prop predictions, NFL betting picks or the best NFL props today , this guide features six player prop bets involving Jordan Love, Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard, Jake Ferguson and more ! NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. While it’s been an impressive start for the Vikings, they have struggled mightily on offense, and aren’t well-equipped to exploit the Dolphins’ weak secondary. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +10.5 Chiefs @ Raiders Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers is one of the best, and perhaps, still one of the most underrated players in the league. Coming off of 13 targets, 10 catches and 116 yards in his season debut, expect another big game from Bowers. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. After favorites wrecked Week 9, the underdogs got out to an early win. I have three early picks for primetime games in Germany, Cincinnati, and Baltimore. Best of luck and enjoy the weekend! Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Lions (-2.5) vs Patriots: O/U 51.5 The Lions and Patriots will meet in Munich, Germany, with a potential shootout on our hands. Last week, Green Bay torched New England’s secondary for almost 400 passing yards, and the Patriots face Detroit, which hasn’t had to throw the last two games. Jared Goff has thrown 25 pass attempts in each of his past two games against the Dolphins and Vikings and gone under 200 yards. Goff hasn’t gone under 200 passing yards in back-to-back games since 2024. Before the previous two games, Goff threw at least 30 passes in six straight and 38 or more in three. This is a spot where I think he clears 30 and could approach 40 pass attempts. The Patriots run the second-most man coverage (28.5%), and that opens the door for this Lions offense. Detroit scored 31 on the Jets, and Goff went 25-of-32 for 269 yards and two touchdowns; and that’s important because that’s the only game that Goff has faced against a team ranked top 10 in man coverage rate. The Patriots are obviously a step up from the Jets defensively, and after the New England secondary was trashed by Jordan Love , Christian Watson , and Matthew Golden last week, this prop just seems that much better. I like Goff Over 34.5 pass attempts up to 35.5. The only quarterback who’s gone for 35-plus against New England is Aaron Rodgers (39) , but that’s about to change. I also added Drake Maye to go Over 33.5 pass attempts and Over 1.5 passing touchdowns. Maye is basically the offense at this point and he has a good matchup with Detroit. The fact that A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson are back helps Maye out, but they aren’t 100-percent, and neither is the Pats offensive line (down 2 starters). Maye has thrown two-plus touchdowns in six-straight games and I think that could continue against a Lions defense that allows a lot of explosives through the air. This could be a shoot out and New England is getting desperate. Picks: Jared Goff Over 34.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Drake Maye Over 33.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Maye over 1.5 Pass TDs (1 unit) Chiefs (-3) at Falcons: O/U 47.5 No Kenneth Walker opens the door for Patrick Mahomes to have a day. The Falcons’ opponents have the ninth-highest pass rate over exception this season, and it’s third if you remove the Buccaneers game where Baker Mayfield threw three times in a monsoon. Atlanta is allowing 228.0 passing yards per game, but remove that Mayfield performance and the number rises to 271.3, which would rank last in the NFL. Here is the list of quarterbacks and how they’ve performed this season against Atlanta. Joe Burrow: 271 Baker Mayfield: 0 Brock Purdy: 288 Caleb Williams: 305 Tyler Huntley: 201 Tyler Shough: 286 Jordan Love: 312 Bryce Young: 287 Aaron Rodgers: 221 Six out of nine quarterbacks went over 240 passing yards, including three of the last four, and six of the past eight. Mahomes has thrown for at least 240 passing yards in five of eight games and two straight. Emmett Johnson has a surprising rushing prop of 71.5 and a rush + rec prop of 102.5, so he may get a heavy dosage, but in a dome setting, I think Kansas City reverts to trusting Mahomes more. I think he adds another to his resume in Atlanta. I’d go up to 244.5. This prop was 236.5 yesterday. Pick: Patrick Mahomes 240+ Passing Yards (1 unit) Jaguars (-10.5) at Titans: O/U 46.5 I lost on Tony Pollard ‘s under rushing yards last week against the Bengals, but will run it back on his Under. Pollard has 129 and 117 rushing yards in back-to-back games on 25 and 21 carries, plus five touchdowns. Both game scripts worked out that Tennessee was in the game until the final whistle, so running the ball was never out of the question. However, that could change here. Not only could the bye week throw off the ground game’s rhythm, but this matchup is the toughest of the season on paper. In the last three games, Derrick Henry was held to 57 rushing yards last week, and Jonathan Taylor to 23 yards two weeks ago, plus Woody Marks had 56 yards. Jacksonville ranks fifth in the NFL with 89.3 rushing yards allowed per game, but that also dropped after Justice Hill had a garbage-time 65-yard run last week. Pollard has hit the over in three straight games and is 5-3 to the over on the season. I’m buying into regression hitting this week. I’m taking the under 58.5 rushing yards down to 53.5. I expect a negative game script and Pollard’s role in the pass game to increase here, and his carries regress back to the norm. Last season, Pollard ran for 60 and 48 yards against the Jaguars on 10 and 14 carries. Jacksonville won by 22 and 34 points. Pick: Tony Pollard Under 58.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Vikings at Packers (-3): O/U 42.5 Did you know that Jordan Love is the only quarterback to throw for two touchdowns against the Vikings this season? That was in Week 1, so seven-straight quarterbacks have thrown for one or fewer touchdowns against Minnesota. Well, fast forward to Week 10, and Green Bay still doesn’t have a running game, so Love has carried the offense. If the Packers are to score more than two touchdowns in this game, it’s hard for me to see it not coming from the arm of Love. He is 8-1 to the over 1.5 passing touchdowns this season. I’ll take him to go Over 1.5 passing touchdowns against Minnesota again and ride his heater of three-straight overs. Outside boundary receivers have had a hard time against Minnesota this season, but one wideout that burned the Vikings defense was Matthew Golden . He’s burned me too. I faded Golden the past two weeks, and he snuck over with 79 yards, then had a monster 164 yards against New England. This becomes a fade spot of a career-high and after catching all 10 targets. I am going under 71.5 yards on Golden, down to 66.5. I’ll root for a red zone touchdown from him, though. Picks: Jordan Love Over 1.5 Passing TDs (1 unit), Matthew Golden Under 71.5 Receiving Yards (1 unit) Steelers at Bengals (-3.5): O/U 49.5 It may be November, but this game will feel like a December or January clash with playoff implications. The Steelers and Bengals are both on four-game winning streaks, and the winner will be in first place in the AFC North. The spread and total for this first game were Bengals -3.5 and 42.5, so we have a full seven-point correction on the total for the second game after Pittsburgh won 30-27 in Week 3. Pittsburgh has been money in years past with Mike Tomlin coming off a bye week (17-5 ML), but this Mike McCarthy’s team now, plus the Bengals, are incredible when at a rest disadvantage. Since 2019 with Zac Taylor , the Bengals are 18-5-1 ATS with a rest disadvantage. Rather than picking a side, I am going under 24.5 points in the first half. The first-half score was 17-17 in Week 3 and flew over the 20.5 first-half total. There could be a lack of rhythm early coming out of the break for the Steelers, and it’ll be hard for the Bengals to replicate or improve on their 7.1-yard play last week against Atlanta. Plus, the Bengals are going off an overseas game, which is never easy on the body. With the intensity of this game early, I like the first half under 24.5 points. Neither team has played anybody good while lighting it up during their four-game win streaks, so the defenses may surprise us. Pick: Steelers vs Bengals 1H Under 24.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Chargers at Ravens (-4.5): O/U 38.5 If you were the Chargers and had to pick an opponent, you’d be picking from the Colts, Dolphins, Eagles, and Ravens at this point (LA lost to the Raiders and Cardinals). This is as good of a matchup for the Chargers offense as it gets. Baltimore has allowed 33-plus points in three straight games, and it might not get better with questionable tags to three starting defensive backs. This is also the Chargers’ first primetime game of the season and first of two or three (Week 15 could get flexed). I think Los Angeles will want this game a little more, and Jim Harbaugh might call up his brother John for any secrets to pull off the win against his former Ravens team. It doesn’t scare me that Jacoby Brissett will be making his Ravens debut in Baltimore on Monday Night Football, because, like I said, that Ravens’ defense has some serious issues. The Chargers finally found the end zone last week after 37 straight drives without a touchdown, and I think they’ll find it more than once in Baltimore. I like the Chargers to get the first cover of the season (0-7-1 ATS), and I think they can win too. Baltimore is 0-4 ATS at home (worst) and 2-7 ATS this season (third-worst). I will take L.A. +4.5. Now the Vikings get their biggest test yet. Here is how I'm wagering the weekend in the professional football ranks. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . Vikings vs. 49ers The Vikings are a different team with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. We saw last weekend that average quarterback play can turn a struggling, inept offense into a group that scores like an average NFL offense. It feels easy to take Minnesota again against San Francisco in Mexico City. However, I'm going to skip the side and total in favor of a prop. The 49ers rely on Christian McCaffrey as the workhorse of their offense, and that was on full display last weekend. He had 13 carries for just over 60 yards and added four catches for 161 yards. I'm targeting his receptions number in this game. The Vikings love to pressure the quarterback, and their blitz and pressure rates are among the highest in NFL history. One way to combat that pressure is to get the running back out of the backfield quickly and find him on mismatches. We saw it last week when McCaffrey got matched up on Von Miller for a touchdown. I think the 49ers have to use McCaffrey in the passing game to have success against Minnesota's pressure. I like the Over on his receptions. Schwartz's Pick: Christian McCaffrey Over 4.5 receptions Buccaneers @ Lions This line could reflect Tampa Bay possibly being without quarterback Baker Mayfield, who is questionable with multiple injuries. However, I believe Mayfield will play, with the Bucs still in the hunt for a division title. He's a tough guy, and he won't miss this game. Even still, I'd still take the Bucs with Jalon Daniels under center. This number is too big. Detroit's defense is without its two best players: Jack Campbell is unavailable, and star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson was injured last week. The Lions' pass rush is significantly worse without Hutchinson, and any team, including the Bucs, will take advantage of it. No Lions lead will be safe moving forward. Tampa Bay has the weapons to score on this defense, and I believe it will. On the other side, there is Detroit's fantastic offense. It's a legitimately good group. However, the Bucs are first in the NFL in defensive EPA per play, even ahead of the Vikings, and they're good at stopping both the run and the pass. They haven't faced an offense quite like the Lions yet, but their defensive production has still been excellent. I believe Tampa Bay's defense can slow down the Lions enough to cover. An NFL player prop is a bet on how an individual player will perform in a game. Common NFL player props include: Passing yards, completions, attempts, and passing touchdowns (quarterbacks). Rushing yards and rushing attempts (running backs, quarterbacks, and other rushers). Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images My early Week 11 NFL player props start with two running backs coming off very different Sundays James Cook broke a 74-yard run for Buffalo, while Christian McCaffrey did most of his damage as a receiver See my three Week 11 NFL prop picks and projected lines below James Cook ran for 157 yards against the Jets. Christian McCaffrey had 161 yards receiving against Dallas. Both performances will draw attention to their Week 11 NFL player props, but I’d approach their rushing totals very differently. Last week, two of my three early targets cleared their projected lines. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 171 receiving yards and Ja’Marr Chase caught 11 passes. McCaffrey fell three rushing yards short, even as he scored three touchdowns. Cook gets Miami in Buffalo, McCaffrey faces Minnesota in Mexico City and Chase visits Washington on Monday night. NFL Player Prop Pick #1: Christian McCaffrey Rushing Yards Christian McCaffrey’s rushing yards have stayed under 74.5 in eight of nine games. His median is 64 yards. Even his best game, a 75-yard afternoon against Arizona, would have beaten my projected line by just half a yard. McCaffrey has had seven, 18 and 13 carries in his last three games. Las Vegas was the one opponent in that stretch against whom he got a steady afternoon of handoffs. He finished with 68 yards. Dallas gave up 161 receiving yards to McCaffrey on just four catches. I want his rushing under if the line opens in the mid-70s: he can hurt Minnesota on a screen or a wheel route without adding a yard to his rushing total. Minnesota has allowed 4.2 yards per carry on 241 attempts. The workload I’d worry about is 18 or 19 carries. At 13, the number he got in Dallas, he’d need a gain of nearly six yards per attempt to beat me. My cutoff matters here. If the opening line lands near the 62 yards he put up in Dallas, I’d pass. In the mid-70s, I’m happy to let his receiving yards grab the headlines. Early Bet: Christian McCaffrey under 74.5 rushing yards (estimated target) NFL Player Prop Pick #2: James Cook Rushing Yards When I compare rushing yards odds , James Cook is the back I want at 89.5. He’s rushed for at least 90 yards in six of nine games, including five of the six in which Buffalo gave him 20 or more carries. Cook has 344 rushing yards on 70 attempts over his last three games. Two of those afternoons show why I’d play the over against Miami, even if the Dolphins keep him from breaking another long touchdown. 74-YARD TD FOR JAMES COOK BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DFRLVP17FL — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Cook’s 74-yard touchdown against the Jets accounted for nearly half of his 157 yards. His other 17 carries went for 83, seven short of what I’m looking for against the Dolphins. The Minnesota game is why I don’t need a repeat of that highlight. Cook’s longest run against the Vikings went for 11 yards. He still finished with 107 because Buffalo went back to him 31 times. Miami has allowed 1,066 rushing yards on 270 attempts, 4.0 per carry, without giving up a run longer than 27 yards in that sample. Teams have kept running on them, which suits how Cook piles up yardage. If Buffalo falls behind and has to throw, the cushion disappears. Cook had just 57 yards on 13 carries in Houston and 75 on 12 against New England. I’m backing him to get closer to his usual workload at home. Early Bet: James Cook over 89.5 rushing yards (estimated target) NFL Player Prop Pick #3: Ja’Marr Chase Receptions For Ja’Marr Chase’s receptions prop against Washington, I’m looking at how quickly Cincinnati’s passing game has shifted. Chase caught 32 passes in his last three games. It took all six of his previous games combined to catch that many. He went for 11 catches against Tennessee, 10 against Atlanta and 11 against Pittsburgh. He’s reached eight in four of nine games overall, so this pick depends on Cincinnati continuing to feed him the way it has over the last three games. The Pittsburgh highlight is the 231 receiving yards. For NFL total receptions props , I give the Atlanta game just as much weight. Chase cleared this target by two catches there without needing anything close to 231 yards. Washington has allowed 217 receptions for 2,341 receiving yards to all positions this season. That total includes backs and tight ends, so it tells us what opponents have done through the air, not which receiver will get the ball. Eight catches is where I’d draw the line for Chase. I’d play the over at 7.5 on Monday night. At 8.5, the price of admission becomes a ninth catch, something Chase managed just once in those first six games. That’s where I’d stop. Here are my eight best bets for the day. Best of luck! Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Titans at Cowboys (-7.5): O/U 54.5 The Titans and Cowboys meet in a battle of two of the worst defenses in the NFL. The Titans are 4-0 to the Over in the last four games, while the Cowboys are 3-1 to the Over in that same span. Dallas is 7-3 to the Over on the year, and Tennessee is 6-3, both ranking top five. The Titans and Cowboys have allowed opponents to score on 46% of drives, ranking 30th and 31st, and both allow a passing success rate of 50% or higher, ranking 29th and 31st — you get the drift. Totals of 54 or higher in the last three seasons are 14-4 to the Over. This one has the making of at least one team reaching 30 points. I like the Over 54.5 up to 55.5. Lean Tennessee +7.5 as they’ve drawn sharp money. Pick: Over 54.5 (1 unit) Jared Goff O/U 32.5 Pass Attempts vs Buccaneers Now that Baker Mayfield is in, we are back on Jared Goff’s passing attempts over 32.5. He would have likely cashed the over 34.5 last week against New England, but Drake Maye’s injury threw off the entire game flow. With Mayfield in, plus the Buccaneers defense being capable of offering resistance in the rush game, this is a good spot for Goff to go over after under his passing attempts in five-straight games. The Bucs run the eighth-most zone coverage at 79.2%, and Goff ranks top 10 in completion percentage (71%), passer rating (100.8), and catchable rate (76.9%) against zone coverage. I’d go up to 33.5. Pick: Jared Goff Over 32.5 Pass Attempts (1.5 units) Patrick Mahomes O/U 30.5 Pass Attempts vs Cardinals Much like Matthew Stafford and the Rams last week, I don’t expect many passes to be thrown in the second half on the Chiefs side. Stafford threw three passes in the third quarter and none in the fourth as the Rams waxed the Cardinals 34-6. With a spread of -15.5, it’s safe to say the Chiefs should be in a positive game script, meaning most of Patrick Mahomes ’ damage will come in the first half. Mahomes threw for 348 yards and a season-high five touchdowns against Atlanta on 22-of-35 (62.9%). The Chiefs’ offense is pretty depleted, and despite not having Kenneth Walker , Emmett Johnson proved he can handle the bulk of the ground work. I like Mahomes to go under 30.5 pass attempts to 29.5. This opened at 31.5. Pick: Patrick Mahomes Under 30.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit) Saquon Barkley O/U 55.5 Rushing Yards vs Steelers Steelers versus Eagles smells like an Under and an offensive struggle. Saquon Barkley ’s props have moved on the move downward over the last few days. This situation is similar to Jonathan Taylo r and the Colts; much like Taylor, Barkley’s snap share and usage will continue to decline as the Eagles lose more games and save him for next season. Barkley had a 58% snap share last week, marking the third time he’s crossed 50%. It won’t happen that often the rest of the season. With less snaps equals less opportunities. The best bet is fading Saquon every week, and I have to lean toward fading the Eagles until they start covering. At 1-8 ATS and 7 straight outright losses. Maybe the bye week helped them, but I doubt it. Pick: Saquon Barkley Under 55.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Saints at Bears (-11.5): O/U 48.5 Chicago coming out of a bye week is certainly an appealing bet-on team. The offense has been cooking with 31, 30, 34, and 27 points since Caleb Williams returned. Those games came against some pretty good defenses too: the Falcons, Patriots, Seahawks, and Buccaneers. The Saints have only allowed three teams to reach 30 points on them: the Lions, Raiders, and Falcons. Better yet, the Saints have played some mediocre passing attacks in the last four games: Bryce Young , Shedeur Sanders , Aaron Rodgers , and Jameis Winston . I don’t think that group has prepared the Saints’ defense for what they’re about to face. The last factor: the Saints are 3-0 ATS on the road this year, but two of those road games came in Weeks 1-2, and the other on October 18 (Week 6). The Saints have either been at home or in Paris in seven of the past eight games. This will be a tough road contest, and if you fall behind early, I don’t think New Orleans could dig themselves out, so I like Chicago -11.5, but love the team total over 29.5 up to 30.5. Pick: Bears Team Total Over 29.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Skattebo recorded 58 or more in six out of seven games he’s received a carry, and posted 124 and 78 in the last two games. This is one of those stinker lines in general; only if the Giants can keep this within a two-possession game could Skattebo hit the over. The Jaguars have a tendency to make teams abandon the run when they start to fall behind. Similar to Tony Pollard with the Titans last week, he was on a mini-monster run, and they were hanging a line that he crushed all season, but went way under versus the Jaguars with nine carries and 33 yards. Pollard had eight receptions on nine targets for 66 yards and a touchdown. I think the Giants’ backs will be important to the pass game because it’s going to be hard to avoid obvious passing or rushing situations. I like Skattebo to go under 54.5 rushing yards, down to 51.5. This week, I would look for a slow start and a lack of points from the Raiders offense, especially after the Brock Bowers injury. Bowers barely practiced on Thursday and is fighting to play, but if he is out, I don’t know if anyone saw the second half last week. yep.title: NFL Week 3 betting guide: Analysis and top plays for Sunday's games
yep.description: Our experts dive into the odds and player props for Week 3 and offer their betting tips and favorite plays.
highlights: Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game-winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 3. I tend to stay away from double-digit spreads in this league (especially for road favorites).

The Bucs have had Robinson on the field on just 23% of clear pass rushing situations this season, down from 52% last year in Carolina. Other sack bets I recommend: Jaelan Phillips UNDER 0.75 sacks (+125) Leonard Williams UNDER 0.25 sacks (-109) Chris Jones UNDER 0.25 sacks (-138) Andrew Van Ginkel UNDER 0.25 sacks (-128) Donovan Ezeiruaku UNDER 4.5 tackles + assists (-107) Ezeiruaku has been playing a little more this season -- 65% of snaps this year vs. 55% last year -- but that's not nearly enough to overcome this high line for an edge rusher. I think what's happening here is this line is being inflated by an outlandish 10-tackle game in Week 1. But it was only the third time Ezeiruaku had ever gone over 4.5 combined tackles in his career.

If Ezeiruaku's role had changed substantially in addition to the slight uptick in playing time this would be a different story, but he's still playing as a 7 or 9 technique 93% of the time (was 89% last year). And Ezeiruaku's tackle rate was almost exactly average for an edge rusher last year. I think the under here is an excellent value. Jordyn Brooks UNDER 9.5 tackles + assists (-116) It's pretty easy to imagine how Brooks could accrue a gaudy tackle number in this game. The Chiefs are double-digit favorites, have been having success with the ground game and if they get out to a big lead they'll simply run the ball to run out the clock. The result? Plenty of tackle opportunities for Miami's defense, and in particular a linebacker like Brooks. But the model knows all that and says this line is just far too high. Just last week Miami was massive underdogs to the 49ers and Brooks recorded just three combined tackles. I would bet this down to -150.
